correctness.summary: After normalizing c to 1, the positive-curvature set has spectrum {t,t^p}. The farthest-point Hessian test gives c>0 and K>=0. On a nonumbilic positive-curvature component, Codazzi gives omega(e1)=e2(t)/(t(1-t^(p-1))) and omega(e2)=p t^(p-2)e1(t)/(1-t^(p-1)); the weak Gauss identity is d omega=-K dmu. The t>1 branch contradicts Stokes. For 0<t<1, a compactly supported cutoff yields a curvature integral bounded by C delta^(p-3) Area{delta<t<2delta}, which tends to zero for all odd p>=3, while dominated convergence sends the same integral to the positive total curvature. Thus t=1 occurs in every positive-curvature component, and rescaling gives curvature c^(-1/(p-1)).

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Cheng proves the p=3 componentwise nonzero-umbilic statement and the exact cubic cutoff formulas. Kühnel-Steller construct rotational generalized Hopf surfaces for kappa=c lambda^alpha, including analytic examples for odd alpha=5,7,9,..., but do not state the arbitrary C3 per-positive-curvature-component forcing theorem. Classical elliptic Weingarten sphere results do not transparently cover the crossing unordered monomial relation. No equivalent higher-odd-power componentwise theorem was located. Residual risk remains from K. Voss (1959), whose full text was not inspected, and from possible later revisions or parallel observations around the very recent Cheng preprint.

value.summary: The theorem extends a key global ingredient of the cubic classification to every higher odd monomial exponent without extra regularity and with arbitrary compact immersions and flat separating regions. It forces one nonzero umbilic in each positive-curvature component, and the proof identifies p=3 as the critical cutoff endpoint while p>3 gains the explicit delta^(p-3) decay. Known nonround analytic generalized Hopf families show that the higher-power cases are nonvacuous.

limitations: No classification of compact odd-power Weingarten surfaces is claimed for p>=5.
Even exponents are not covered because the global nonnegativity argument for Gaussian curvature uses odd p.
The immersion is assumed C3; no lower regularity version is established.
Higher odd-power rotational examples are known already; this record does not claim a new construction.
The full text of Voss (1959) was not inspected, leaving a residual historical originality risk.
The motivating cubic preprint is very recent, so later revisions or unindexed parallel observations may overlap.
Independent audit has not been performed.
